Body.raw:
Unify the "operate on all todos" idiom to ONE form: an `ALL` positional-selector
sentinel, replacing the `--all` flag on `doctor` and `log`.

Why (from the 2026-07-25 design discussion):
- The selector grammar collapses to a single positional slot: self | curr |
  <id-prefix> | ALL. `doctor ALL`, `log ALL`, and any future sweeper read
  identically.
- It mirrors the existing `--states=ALL` uppercase-macro convention already in
  this codebase (uppercase = "the whole set"), so `doctor ALL` echoes
  `--states=ALL`. One word, one meaning.
- It drops a special flag instead of adding flag surface, and composes:
  `search ... --states=ALL` and `doctor ALL` share the word.

Scope:
- Selector resolution recognizes the uppercase sentinel `ALL` as "every todo in
  the corpus" (alongside self/curr and id prefixes). `ALL` is reserved (ids are
  hex, so no collision).
- `doctor ALL` replaces `doctor --all` (sweep the whole corpus / audit + repair
  + schema sweep + auto-tag recompute across all todos).
- `log ALL` replaces `log --all` (render every root as a forest).
- Remove the `--all` argparse flag (dest sweep_all) from both commands.
- Update help strings and SKILL.md (the doctor/log CLI rows + the Selectors
  section) to document the `ALL` sentinel.
- Update tests: `doctor --all` -> `doctor ALL`, `log --all` -> `log ALL`; add a
  case asserting `--all` is no longer accepted.

Non-goals:
- `ls` / `search` are unchanged -- they are the inherent "null-query = all" case
  and take no selector (consistent with Unix listing norms).
- No other subcommand gains an ALL mode.

Working model: worked per skills/projectmanagement/PLAN.md (Opus orchestrator /
Sonnet implementor); the AC is a frozen test.
